query: What practical approximation of Bayesian surprise is suitable for large pretrained models given compute limits, and how do we measure its calibration cost?

response.query: What practical approximation of Bayesian surprise is suitable for large pretrained models given compute limits, and how do we measure its calibration cost?
response.answer: For large models, approximate Bayesian surprise using Monte Carlo sampling with a small number of samples. Measure calibration cost by comparing predicted and actual log-likelihoods.

results.title: Proceedings of the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods ...
results.content: This paper presents a novel neural machine translation model which jointly learns translation and source-side latent graph representations of sentences. Unlike existing pipelined approaches using syntactic parsers, our end-to-end model learns a latent graph parser as part of the encoder of an attention-based neural machine translation model, and thus the parser is optimized according to the translation objective. We show that small and shallow feed-forward neural networks can achieve near state-of-the-art results on a range of unstructured and structured language processing tasks while being considerably cheaper in memory and computational requirements than deep recurrent models. We propose a novel LSTM-based deep multi-task learning framework for aspect term extraction from user review sentences. In this paper, we present a simple yet effective method for learning word embeddings based on text from different domains. Our approach outperforms both standard techniques like LDA and a state-of-the-art graph-based method, and provides promising initial results for this new task in computational social science.
